report: Friday, 27 November. A quiet day for the account. The trader did not trade. The quotes it saw were last night's closing prices, about 15 hours old. No news item was a primary-source, name-specific new event. Both are hard rules, so standing aside followed the rules. It was not a call on the market. In the markets, tariff fears eased and the Euro Stoxx 50 rose about 2 percent. Brent sat at 92.38 dollars, below our 98 dollar trigger, and the OPEC+ outcome is still unknown. Gold bounced to 3681.9. Copper futures jumped about 6.7 percent, and that move still needs checking against the previous close. There were no orders, no fills and no costs. There are no open positions, so no exit dates or stops to watch. The day result is zero. Equity is 1969.83 euros, down 1.51 percent in total, all from the one Infineon loss. Reconcile is consistent. Two odd things. The trader said it sent shadow calls on Stellantis down and ASML up, but the system rejected both, so they will not be scored. And the quotes were stale again, which blocks any entry. On luck versus skill: down shadow calls are 7 for 7 and up calls 1 for 10. That mostly reflects a falling market, not proven skill. One flat day shows nothing.
questions: Why did the system reject the STLAP.PA down and ASML.AS up shadow calls, and was the trader told so it does not count them as pending?

The trader keeps seeing quotes 15 or more hours old at decision time. Should the run move to a time when delayed live quotes exist, or is a no-trade rule on stale quotes costing us every chance to act?
Down shadows are 7 for 7 in a falling market and up shadows 1 for 10. How should we separate a real edge from market direction before letting either pattern loosen or tighten the entry rules?

lessons.rule: Up calls on an already-published or secondary-source company event, made into a falling sector, lose money; such a call needs a primary-source new event (5+ cases, tightens the catalyst test).
